concepts.title: Meaning and Functions of Money
concepts.definition: Money is anything that is generally accepted as a medium of exchange, a store of value, a unit of account and a standard of deferred payment.
concepts.key_idea: Money removes the inefficiencies of barter by serving as a common medium of exchange.
question_patterns: Define Meaning and Functions of Money and explain its components.
Distinguish between related terms in Introduction.
Compute Meaning and Functions of Money given numerical data.
Explain the significance of Meaning and Functions of Money in national income accounting.
Identify the correct formula and apply it to a problem on Meaning and Functions of Money.

solution_steps.explain: Money is a generally acceptable medium of exchange.
Medium of exchange and measure of value.
Store of value and standard of deferred payment.

worked_examples.question: Explain the four functions of money.
worked_examples.solution: Medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value and standard of deferred payment.

worked_examples.question: How does money solve the problem of double coincidence of wants?
worked_examples.solution: By acting as a universally accepted medium, money eliminates the need for direct barter.
worked_examples.answer: Money removes double coincidence of wants.

exercises.question: Define money and list its primary functions.
Explain how money acts as a store of value.

concepts.title: Types of Money
concepts.definition: Money can be classified as commodity money, metallic money, paper money, bank money (deposits), fiduciary money and credit money.
concepts.key_idea: Modern economies use a mix of fiat paper money, coins and bank-deposit money.
question_patterns: Define Types of Money and explain its components.
Distinguish between related terms in Forms of Money.
Compute Types of Money given numerical data.
Explain the significance of Types of Money in national income accounting.
Identify the correct formula and apply it to a problem on Types of Money.

solution_steps.explain: Money whose value equals the commodity it is made of.
Money declared legal tender by government decree.
Demand deposits withdrawable by cheque are bank money.

worked_examples.question: Distinguish between commodity money and fiat money.
worked_examples.solution: Commodity money has intrinsic value; fiat money has value by legal decree.
worked_examples.answer: Commodity money is backed by the commodity; fiat money by law.

worked_examples.question: Give an example of bank money.
worked_examples.solution: Demand deposits that can be withdrawn by cheque.

exercises.question: List the different types of money with one example each.
Explain the concept of legal tender money.

concepts.title: Money Supply: M1, M2, M3, M4
concepts.definition: Money supply is the total stock of money circulating in the economy, measured by RBI in four measures: M1, M2, M3 and M4.
concepts.formula: M1 = Currency + Demand Deposits + Other Deposits with RBI
concepts.key_idea: M1 is the narrowest and most liquid measure; M4 is the broadest and least liquid.
question_patterns: Define Money Supply: M1, M2, M3, M4 and explain its components.
Distinguish between related terms in Money Supply.
Compute Money Supply: M1, M2, M3, M4 given numerical data.
Explain the significance of Money Supply: M1, M2, M3, M4 in national income accounting.
Identify the correct formula and apply it to a problem on Money Supply: M1, M2, M3, M4.

solution_steps.explain: Sum currency held by the public and demand deposits.

solution_steps.action: Add post office savings for M2
solution_steps.explain: M2 = M1 + savings deposits with post office.

solution_steps.action: Add time deposits for M3 and post office deposits for M4
solution_steps.explain: M3 = M1 + time deposits; M4 = M3 + all post office deposits.
solution_steps.compute: M3 = M1 + TD; M4 = M3 + Post office deposits

worked_examples.question: Currency = Rs 1,000, demand deposits = Rs 2,000, other deposits with RBI = Rs 50. Find M1.
If M1 = Rs 5,000 and time deposits = Rs 3,000, find M3.

exercises.question: Define money supply and list its four measures.
Compute M1: currency 2000, demand deposits 4000, other deposits 100.

concepts.title: Functions of the Central Bank (RBI)
concepts.definition: The Reserve Bank of India is the apex monetary authority that issues currency, acts as banker to the government and banks, controls credit and manages foreign exchange.
concepts.key_idea: The central bank regulates the banking system and formulates monetary policy.
question_patterns: Define Functions of the Central Bank (RBI) and explain its components.
Distinguish between related terms in Central Banking.
Compute Functions of the Central Bank (RBI) given numerical data.
Explain the significance of Functions of the Central Bank (RBI) in national income accounting.
Identify the correct formula and apply it to a problem on Functions of the Central Bank (RBI).

solution_steps.explain: RBI has the sole right to issue currency notes.
RBI acts as banker to the government and as lender of last resort to banks.
RBI controls money supply and credit through monetary policy.

worked_examples.question: Explain the role of RBI as lender of last resort.
worked_examples.solution: When commercial banks cannot meet their requirements, RBI provides funds to prevent failure.
worked_examples.answer: RBI supports banks in liquidity crises.

worked_examples.question: Why is RBI called the banker to the government?
worked_examples.solution: It manages government accounts, issues loans and manages public debt.
worked_examples.answer: RBI handles government banking and debt management.

exercises.question: List any four functions of the Reserve Bank of India.
Explain the role of RBI as the controller of credit.

concepts.title: Monetary Policy
concepts.definition: Monetary policy is the policy through which the central bank regulates money supply and credit to achieve price stability and growth.
concepts.key_idea: Monetary policy uses quantitative and qualitative instruments to influence credit availability.
question_patterns: Define Monetary Policy and explain its components.
Distinguish between related terms in Central Banking.
Compute Monetary Policy given numerical data.
Explain the significance of Monetary Policy in national income accounting.
Identify the correct formula and apply it to a problem on Monetary Policy.

solution_steps.explain: Policy regulating money supply and interest rates.
Price stability, growth, exchange stability and employment.
Quantitative (bank rate, CRR, SLR, open market operations) and qualitative (margin, moral suasion).

worked_examples.question: Distinguish between quantitative and qualitative instruments of monetary policy.
worked_examples.solution: Quantitative tools affect total credit volume; qualitative tools direct credit to specific sectors.
worked_examples.answer: Quantitative affects volume; qualitative affects direction of credit.

worked_examples.question: What is the primary objective of monetary policy in India?
worked_examples.solution: To control inflation and support economic growth.

exercises.question: Define monetary policy and state its main objectives.
Explain any two quantitative instruments of monetary policy.

concepts.title: Functions of Commercial Banks
concepts.definition: Commercial banks accept deposits, grant loans and advances, and provide agency and general utility services.
concepts.key_idea: Commercial banks mobilise savings and channel them into productive investment.
question_patterns: Define Functions of Commercial Banks and explain its components.
Distinguish between related terms in Commercial Banking.
Compute Functions of Commercial Banks given numerical data.
Explain the significance of Functions of Commercial Banks in national income accounting.
Identify the correct formula and apply it to a problem on Functions of Commercial Banks.

solution_steps.explain: Accepting deposits and lending loans.
Agency services like collection of cheques and utility services like lockers.
Banks bridge savers and investors in the economy.

worked_examples.question: List the primary functions of a commercial bank.
worked_examples.solution: Accepting demand and time deposits and granting loans and advances.
worked_examples.answer: Deposits and loans are primary functions.

worked_examples.question: Give two agency functions of a commercial bank.
worked_examples.solution: Collection of cheques and bills, and payment of insurance premiums on behalf of customers.
worked_examples.answer: Agency services are performed on behalf of customers.

exercises.question: Explain the primary functions of commercial banks.
Give two general utility services of commercial banks.

concepts.title: Credit Creation by Commercial Banks
concepts.definition: Credit creation is the process by which banks create deposits many times the initial deposit through the fractional reserve system.
concepts.formula: Credit multiplier = 1 / LRR; Total credit = Initial deposit x multiplier
concepts.key_idea: Banks keep a fraction of deposits as reserves and lend the rest, multiplying total credit.
question_patterns: Define Credit Creation by Commercial Banks and explain its components.
Distinguish between related terms in Commercial Banking.
Compute Credit Creation by Commercial Banks given numerical data.
Explain the significance of Credit Creation by Commercial Banks in national income accounting.
Identify the correct formula and apply it to a problem on Credit Creation by Commercial Banks.

solution_steps.explain: The primary deposit received by the bank.
LRR is the fraction of deposits banks must keep as reserves.
Multiply initial deposit by the credit multiplier.

worked_examples.question: Initial deposit = Rs 1,000, LRR = 10%. Find total credit created.
If LRR = 20% and initial deposit = Rs 2,000, find the credit multiplier and total credit.

exercises.question: Explain the process of credit creation by commercial banks.
Compute total credit: initial deposit 5000, LRR 25%.

concepts.title: Instruments of Monetary Policy
concepts.definition: Instruments of monetary policy are the tools used by RBI to control money supply and credit: bank rate, repo rate, reverse repo rate, CRR, SLR and open market operations.
concepts.key_idea: Quantitative instruments influence overall credit; qualitative instruments guide its direction.
question_patterns: Define Instruments of Monetary Policy and explain its components.
Distinguish between related terms in Central Banking.
Compute Instruments of Monetary Policy given numerical data.
Explain the significance of Instruments of Monetary Policy in national income accounting.
Identify the correct formula and apply it to a problem on Instruments of Monetary Policy.

solution_steps.explain: Bank rate, repo rate, reverse repo rate, CRR, SLR and open market operations.
Margin requirements, moral suasion and direct action.
Tightening reduces credit; easing expands credit.

worked_examples.question: Explain how an increase in the bank rate affects credit.
worked_examples.solution: Higher bank rate raises lending rates, reducing borrowing and credit.
worked_examples.answer: Credit contracts when the bank rate rises.

worked_examples.question: What are open market operations?
worked_examples.solution: Buying and selling of government securities by RBI to control money supply.
worked_examples.answer: OMO regulates money supply via securities trading.

exercises.question: Define bank rate and repo rate.
Explain open market operations and their effect on money supply.

concepts.title: Banking System in India
concepts.definition: The Indian banking system comprises the RBI, commercial banks (public, private, foreign) and cooperative banks, supported by recent reforms and digital banking initiatives.
concepts.key_idea: India's banking structure is a three-tier system led by the RBI.
question_patterns: Define Banking System in India and explain its components.
Distinguish between related terms in Banking System.
Compute Banking System in India given numerical data.
Explain the significance of Banking System in India in national income accounting.
Identify the correct formula and apply it to a problem on Banking System in India.

solution_steps.explain: RBI sits at the top of the banking structure.
Public, private and foreign banks form the second tier.
Cooperative banks serve rural and urban local needs.

worked_examples.question: Describe the three-tier structure of the Indian banking system.
worked_examples.solution: RBI at the top, commercial banks in the middle, and cooperative banks at the base.
worked_examples.answer: Three-tier: RBI, commercial banks, cooperative banks.

worked_examples.question: Name two recent developments in Indian banking.
worked_examples.solution: Digital banking and the growth of payment banks and small finance banks.
worked_examples.answer: Digital and differentiated banks are recent developments.

exercises.question: Outline the structure of the Indian banking system.
Name two types of commercial banks in India.
